notes.title: 2.3.4 - Implement Physical Security Countermeasures
notes.html:
Lab Steps — Easy Version

  1. 1. Install Smart Card Readers

    1. Go to Shelf.
    2. Expand Door Locks.
    3. Drag Smart Card Reader to the highlighted spot outside the building's front door.
    4. Drag another Smart Card Reader to the highlighted spot outside the Networking Closet door.

  2. 2. Install IP Security Cameras

    1. Go to Shelf.
    2. Expand CCTV Cameras.
    3. Drag IP Security Camera to the highlighted circle inside the Networking Closet.
    4. Drag another IP Security Camera to just outside the Networking Closet.

  3. 3. Install Restricted Access Sign

    1. Go to Shelf.
    2. Expand Restricted Access Signs.
    3. Drag Restricted Access Sign onto the Networking Closet door.

  4. 4. Place Visitor Log

    1. Go to Shelf.
    2. Expand Visitor Logs.
    3. Drag Visitor Log onto the Lobby desk.

  5. Final Check

    You should have installed 6 total items:

    1. Smart Card Reader — Front door
    2. Smart Card Reader — Networking Closet door
    3. IP Security Camera — Inside Networking Closet
    4. IP Security Camera — Outside Networking Closet
    5. Restricted Access Sign — Networking Closet door
    6. Visitor Log — Lobby desk

notes.title: 2.4.6 - Configure a Captive Portal
notes.html:
Lab Steps — Easy Version

  1. Sign Into pfSense

    1. In Username, enter admin.

    2. In Password, enter P@ssw0rd. The 0 is a zero.

    3. Click SIGN IN or press Enter.

  2. Add the Captive Portal Zone

    1. At the top, go to Services > Captive Portal.

    2. Click Add.

    3. For Zone name, enter WiFi-Guest.

    4. For Zone description, enter Guest wireless access zone.

    5. Click Save & Continue.

  3. Enable and Configure the Captive Portal

    1. Under Captive Portal Configuration, check Enable.

    2. For Interfaces, select GuestWi-Fi.

    3. For Maximum concurrent connections, enter 50.

    4. For Idle timeout, enter 15.

    5. For Hard timeout, enter 45.

    6. Scroll down and check Per-user bandwidth restriction.

    7. For Default download (Kbit/s), enter 7000.

    8. For Default upload (Kbit/s), enter 2400.

    9. Under Authentication, select None, don't authenticate users.

    10. Scroll to the bottom and click Save.

  4. Allow the MAC Address

    1. Go back to the Captive Portal page.

    2. Click the Edit Zone pencil icon.

    3. Under the Services breadcrumb, click MACs.

    4. Click Add.

    5. Make sure Action is set to Pass.

    6. For Mac Address, enter 00:00:1C:11:22:33.

    7. Click Save.

  5. Allow the IP Address

    1. Under the Services breadcrumb, click Allowed IP Addresses.

    2. Click Add.

    3. For IP Address, enter 198.28.1.100.

    4. From the IP address drop-down, select 16.

    5. For Description, enter Security analyst's laptop.

    6. Make sure Direction is set to Both.

    7. Click Save.

  6. Final Check

    You should have:

    1. Zone name — WiFi-Guest

    2. Description — Guest wireless access zone

    3. Captive Portal — Enabled

    4. Interface — GuestWi-Fi

    5. Maximum connections — 50

    6. Idle timeout — 15 minutes

    7. Hard timeout — 45 minutes

    8. Per-user bandwidth restriction — Enabled

    9. Download — 7000 Kbit/s

    10. Upload — 2400 Kbit/s

    11. Authentication — None, don't authenticate users

    12. MAC Action — Pass

    13. MAC Address — 00:00:1C:11:22:33

    14. Allowed IP — 198.28.1.100/16

    15. IP Description — Security analyst's laptop

    16. IP Direction — Both

versions.html:
Lab Steps — Easy Version

  1. Sign Into pfSense

    1. In Username, enter admin.

    2. In Password, enter P@ssw0rd. The 0 is a zero.

    3. Click SIGN IN or press Enter.

  2. Add the Captive Portal Zone

    1. At the top, go to Services > Captive Portal.

    2. Click Add.

    3. For Zone name, enter WiFi-Guest.

    4. For Zone description, enter Guest wireless access zone.

    5. Click Save & Continue.

  3. Enable and Configure the Captive Portal

    1. Under Captive Portal Configuration, check Enable.

    2. For Interfaces, select GuestWi-Fi.

    3. For Maximum concurrent connections, enter 50.

    4. For Idle timeout, enter 15.

    5. For Hard timeout, enter 45.

    6. Scroll down and check Per-user bandwidth restriction.

    7. For Default download (Kbit/s), enter 7000.

    8. For Default upload (Kbit/s), enter 2400.

    9. Under Authentication, select None, don't authenticate users.

    10. Scroll to the bottom and click Save.

  4. Allow the MAC Address

    1. Go back to the Captive Portal page.

    2. Click the Edit Zone pencil icon.

    3. Under the Services breadcrumb, click MACs.

    4. Click Add.

    5. Make sure Action is set to Pass.

    6. For Mac Address, enter 00:00:1C:11:22:33.

    7. Click Save.

  5. Allow the IP Address

    1. Under the Services breadcrumb, click Allowed IP Addresses.

    2. Click Add.

    3. For IP Address, enter 198.28.1.100.

    4. From the IP address drop-down, select 16.

    5. For Description, enter Security analyst's laptop.

    6. Make sure Direction is set to Both.

    7. Click Save.

notes.title: 2.4.7 - Discover Bluetooth Devices
notes.html:
Lab Steps — Easy Version

  1. Find and Enable the Bluetooth Adapter

    1. Open Terminal.

    2. Type:

    hciconfig

    1. Press Enter.

    2. Find the Bluetooth adapter named hci0.

    3. If hci0 shows DOWN, type:

    hciconfig hci0 up

    1. Press Enter.

    2. Type:

    hciconfig

    1. Press Enter.

    2. Make sure hci0 now shows UP RUNNING.

  2. Find All Bluetooth Devices

    1. Type:

    hcitool scan

    1. Press Enter.

    2. Wait for the scan to finish.

    3. Look at the MAC address and device name for each device.

    4. Count how many devices appear.

    5. Use this information to answer Question 1.

  3. Check Which Devices Are Alive and in Range

    1. Take the MAC address of each device from the scan.

    2. Type:

    l2ping MAC-ADDRESS

    1. Replace MAC-ADDRESS with the actual address of the device.

    2. Press Enter.

    3. If you see bytes from, the device is alive and in range.

    4. Press Ctrl + C to stop the ping.

    5. Repeat for all devices.

    6. Count how many devices responded.

    7. Use this information to answer Question 2.

  4. Find the Services on Francisco's Dell Laptop

    1. Find Francisco's Dell Precision Laptop from the scan.

    2. His MAC address is:

    AF:52:23:92:EF:AF

    1. Type:

    sdptool browse AF:52:23:92:EF:AF

    1. Press Enter.

    2. Look through the results for the available Service Name entries.

    3. Use the service results to answer Question 3.

  5. Find Brian's Braven Speaker Information

    1. Find Brian's Braven Speaker from the scan.

    2. Brian's MAC address is:

    BB:1A:7D:D4:44:19

    1. Type:

    hcitool inq

    1. Press Enter.

    2. Find the line containing:

    BB:1A:7D:D4:44:19

    1. Look for the clock offset.

    2. Look for the class.

    3. Use the class to answer Question 4.


  6. Final Check

    You should have completed:

    1. Bluetooth adapter discovered using hciconfig

    2. hci0 changed from DOWN to UP RUNNING

    3. Bluetooth devices discovered using hcitool scan

    4. Devices tested using l2ping

    5. Francisco's laptop queried using sdptool

    6. Brian's speaker checked using hcitool inq

    7. All 4 lab questions answered


    Lab Questions and Answers

  7. Question 1

    As a result of the scan, how many devices were found?

    A. 3
    B. 4
    C. 5
    D. 6
    E. 7

    Answer: D. 6 ✅

  8. Question 2

    How many of the devices scanned were alive and in range?

    Answer: 6 ✅

  9. Question 3

    Which service searches were successful on Francisco's Dell Laptop? (Select two.)

    A. Ad Hoc User Service
    B. Device ID Service Record
    C. Service Discovery
    D. CDP Proximal Transport

    Answer: A. Ad Hoc User Service ✅
    Answer: B. Device ID Service Record ✅

  10. Question 4

    Using the MAC address, what is the class ID number for Brian's Braven Speaker?

    A. 0x5a020c
    B. 0x2985
    C. 0x248080
    D. 0x5634135
    E. 0x460100

    Answer: C. 0x248080 ✅



  11. How We Got the Answers

  12. Question 1 — 6 Devices

    We ran:

    hcitool scan

    The scan showed these 6 devices:

    1. Pascal's Galaxy Note20 Ultra 5G

    2. Peter's MacBook Air

    3. Brian's Braven Speaker

    4. Wendy's iPhone Pro

    5. Francisco's Dell Precision Laptop

    6. Amelie's Galaxy Note10

    Therefore:

    Answer = 6

  13. Question 2 — 6 Alive and in Range

    We used:

    l2ping MAC-ADDRESS

    We tested the devices and received responses such as:

    44 bytes from

    The tests also showed 0% loss, meaning the devices responded and were alive and within Bluetooth range.

    Therefore:

    Answer = 6

  14. Question 3 — Ad Hoc User Service and Device ID Service Record

    We ran:

    sdptool browse AF:52:23:92:EF:AF

    This queried Francisco's Dell Precision Laptop.

    The results showed the service records needed for the question, including:

    Service Name: Device ID Service Record

    and:

    Service Name: Ad Hoc User Service

    Therefore:

    Answers = Ad Hoc User Service and Device ID Service Record

  15. Question 4 — 0x248080

    We first identified Brian's Braven Speaker MAC address:

    BB:1A:7D:D4:44:19

    Then we ran:

    hcitool inq

    The results showed:

    BB:1A:7D:D4:44:19    clock offset: 0x323c    class: 0x248080

    Brian's class ID is therefore:

    Answer = 0x248080 ✅

notes.title: 2.4.8 - Secure a Mobile Device
notes.html:
Lab Steps — Easy Version

  1. Set Require Passcode to 5 Minutes

    1. On the iPad, open Settings.

    2. On the left side, select Touch ID & Passcode.

    3. Enter the current passcode:

    3141

    1. On the right side, select Require Passcode.

    2. Select After 5 minutes.

  2. Turn Off Simple Passcode

    1. At the top, select Passcode Lock.

    2. Find Simple Passcode.

    3. Slide the switch OFF.

    4. Enter the current passcode:

    3141

    1. Enter the new passcode:

    youwontguessthisone

    1. Select Next.

    2. Enter the new passcode again:

    youwontguessthisone

    1. Select Done.

  3. Enable Erase Data

    1. Go back to Touch ID & Passcode.

    2. Find Erase Data.

    3. Slide the switch ON.

    4. When the warning appears, select Enable.

    5. The iPad will now erase its data after 10 failed passcode attempts.

  4. Final Check

    You should have configured:

    1. Simple Passcode — OFF

    2. New Passcode — youwontguessthisone

    3. Require Passcode — After 5 minutes

    4. Erase Data — ON

    5. Erase after — 10 failed passcode attempts

notes.title: 2.4.9 - Configure a Security Appliance
notes.html:
Lab Steps — Easy Version


  1. 1. Sign Into pfSense

    1. Open the web browser.

    2. In the address bar, enter:

    198.28.56.22

    1. Press Enter.

    2. For Username, enter:

    admin

    1. For Password, enter:

    pfsense

    1. Select SIGN IN.

  2. 2. Add the Primary DNS Server

    1. From the pfSense menu, go to System > General Setup.

    2. Find the DNS Server Settings section.

    3. In the first DNS Server field, enter:

    163.128.78.93

    1. For its Hostname, enter:

    DNS1

  3. 3. Add the Secondary DNS Server

    1. In the second DNS Server field, enter:

    163.128.80.93

    1. For its Hostname, enter:

    DNS2

    1. Scroll to the bottom.

    2. Select Save.

  4. 4. Open the WAN Interface

    1. From the pfSense menu, go to Interfaces > WAN.

    2. Find General Configuration.

    3. Check Enable interface.

    4. Find IPv4 Configuration Type.

    5. Select Static IPv4.

  5. 5. Configure the Static IPv4 Address

    1. Find Static IPv4 Configuration.

    2. For IPv4 Address, enter:

    65.86.24.136

    1. For the subnet/prefix drop-down, select:

    8

    1. The complete address should be:

    65.86.24.136/8

  6. 6. Add the WAN Gateway

    1. Find the IPv4 Upstream Gateway or gateway option.

    2. Select Add a new gateway.

    3. For Type, select Default gateway.

    4. For Name, enter:

    WANGateway

    1. For Gateway IP Address, enter:

    65.86.1.1

    1. Select Add or Save to add the gateway.

  7. 7. Save the WAN Configuration

    1. Make sure the new WANGateway is selected for the WAN interface.

    2. Scroll to the bottom.

    3. Select Save.

    4. If Apply Changes appears, select Apply Changes.

  8. Final Check

    You should have configured:

    1. pfSense URL — 198.28.56.22

    2. Username — admin

    3. Primary DNS — 163.128.78.93

    4. Primary DNS Hostname — DNS1

    5. Secondary DNS — 163.128.80.93

    6. Secondary DNS Hostname — DNS2

    7. WAN Interface — Enabled

    8. IPv4 Configuration — Static IPv4

    9. WAN IPv4 Address — 65.86.24.136/8

    10. Gateway Type — Default gateway

    11. Gateway Name — WANGateway

    12. Gateway IP Address — 65.86.1.1

Lab Steps — Easy Version

  1. 1. Sign Into pfSense

    1. Open Google Chrome.

    2. Maximize the window.

    198.28.56.22

    1. Press Enter.

    2. For Username, enter:

    admin

    1. For Password, enter:

    pfsense

    1. Click SIGN IN.

  2. 2. Change the Admin Password

    1. From the top menu, go to System > User Manager.

    2. Find the admin account.

    3. Under Actions, click the Edit user pencil icon.

    4. For Password, enter:

    Donttre@donme

    1. For Confirm Password, enter:

    Donttre@donme

    1. Scroll to the bottom.

    2. Click Save.

  3. 3. Create the New Administrative User

    1. From System > User Manager, click Add.

    2. For Username, enter:

    lyoung

    1. For Password, enter:

    C@nyouGuess!t

    1. For Confirm Password, enter:

    C@nyouGuess!t

    1. For Full Name, enter:

    Liam Young

    1. Find Group Membership.

    2. Select admins.

    3. Click Move to Member of list.

    4. Make sure admins appears in the member list.

    5. Scroll to the bottom.

    6. Click Save.

  4. 4. Set the Session Timeout to 20 Minutes

    1. Stay in System > User Manager.

    2. Under the System breadcrumb/navigation, click Settings.

    3. Find Session timeout.

    4. Enter:

    20

    1. Click Save.

  5. 5. Change webConfigurator to HTTP

    1. From the top menu, go to System > Advanced.

    2. Make sure you are on the Admin Access tab.

    3. Find the webConfigurator section.

    4. Under Protocol, select HTTP.

    5. Do not change the TCP port.

  6. 6. Disable the webConfigurator Anti-Lockout Rule

    1. Stay on System > Advanced > Admin Access.

    2. Scroll down until you find Anti-lockout.

    3. Check:

    ☑ Disable webConfigurator anti-lockout rule

    1. Do not change Threshold, Blocktime, or Detection time.

    2. Scroll to the bottom.

    3. Click Save.

    Final Check

    You should have configured:

    1. Admin password — Donttre@donme

    2. New username — lyoung

    3. New user password — C@nyouGuess!t

    4. Full Name — Liam Young

    5. Group Membership — admins

    6. Session timeout — 20 minutes

    7. webConfigurator Protocol — HTTP

    8. Disable webConfigurator anti-lockout rule — Checked

    9. All changes — Saved

notes.title: 2.5.5 - Analyze Passwords using Rainbow Tables
notes.html:
Lab Steps — Easy Version

1. Find the Correct Charset

  1. Open Terminal.

  2. Type:

cat /usr/share/rainbowcrack/charset.txt

  1. Press Enter.

  2. Look through the charset list.

  3. The correct charset is:

ascii-32-95

  1. Select Answer Questions.

  2. For Question 1, enter ascii-32-95.

2. Create the MD5 Rainbow Table

  1. Go back to Terminal.

  2. Type:

rtgen md5 ascii-32-95 1 20 0 1000 1000 0

  1. Press Enter.

  2. Wait for it to finish.

3. Create the SHA1 Rainbow Table

  1. Type:

rtgen sha1 ascii-32-95 1 20 0 1000 1000 0

  1. Press Enter.

  2. Wait for it to finish.

4. Sort the Rainbow Tables

  1. Type:

rtsort .

  1. Press Enter.

  2. Wait for both rainbow tables to finish sorting.

5. Crack the Password Hashes

  1. Type:

rcrack . -l /root/captured_hashes.txt

  1. Make sure -l is a lowercase L, not the number 1.

  2. Press Enter.

  3. Wait for the cracking process to finish.

  4. Use the results to answer Questions 2–5.

Lab Questions and Answers

Question 1

Which charset supports the company's password requirements?

Answer: ascii-32-95

Question 2

What is the password for hash 202cb962ac59075b964b07152d234b70?

Answer: lmnop

Question 3

What is the password for hash 400238780e6c41f8f790161e6ed4df3b?

Answer: S3cur3Dev!ce

Question 4

What is the password for hash 89BF04763BF91C9EE2DDBE23D7B5C730BDD41FF2?

Answer: DisneyL@nd3

Question 5

Which of the passwords found do not meet the company's password policy?

Answer: lmnop

How We Got the Answers

Question 1: The cat command displayed the available RainbowCrack charsets. ascii-32-95 contains the uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters required by the company's password policy.

Questions 2–4: We created MD5 and SHA1 rainbow tables with rtgen, sorted them with rtsort ., and then compared the captured hashes against those tables using rcrack. The matches gave us lmnop, S3cur3Dev!ce, and DisneyL@nd3.

Question 5: lmnop fails the password policy because it is only 5 characters long, has no uppercase letter, and has no required special character.

Final Check

  1. Charset — ascii-32-95

  2. MD5 rainbow table — Created

  3. SHA1 rainbow table — Created

  4. Rainbow tables — Sorted

  5. Hashes — Cracked

  6. Q1 — ascii-32-95

  7. Q2 — lmnop

  8. Q3 — S3cur3Dev!ce

  9. Q4 — DisneyL@nd3

  10. Q5 — lmnop

  11. Select Score Lab.

notes.title: 2.5.6 - Configure Account Password Policies
notes.html:
Lab Steps — Easy Version


1. Open Local Security Policy

  1. Select Start.

  2. Open Windows Administrative Tools.

  3. Select Local Security Policy.

  4. Maximize the window.

  5. On the left, expand Account Policies.


2. Remember the Last 4 Passwords

  1. Select Password Policy.

  2. Double-click Enforce password history.

  3. Enter:

4

  1. Select OK.


3. Force Password Changes Every 30 Days

  1. Double-click Maximum password age.

  2. Enter:

30

  1. Select OK.


4. Prevent Password Changes for 2 Days

  1. Double-click Minimum password age.

  2. Enter:

2

  1. Select OK.


5. Require at Least 10 Characters

  1. Double-click Minimum password length.

  2. Enter:

10

  1. Select OK.


6. Require Complex Passwords

  1. Double-click Password must meet complexity requirements.

  2. Select Enabled.

  3. Select OK.


7. Open Account Lockout Policy

  1. On the left, under Account Policies, select Account Lockout Policy.


8. Lock the Account After 4 Wrong Attempts

  1. Double-click Account lockout threshold.

  2. Enter:

4

  1. Select OK.

  2. If Windows shows a Suggested Value Changes message, select OK.

  3. We will manually set the correct values next.


9. Unlock the Account After 60 Minutes

  1. Double-click Account lockout duration.

  2. Enter:

60

  1. Select OK.


10. Reset the Failed Attempt Counter After 40 Minutes

  1. Double-click Reset account lockout counter after.

  2. Enter:

40

  1. Select OK.


Final Check

Make sure everything shows:

  1. Enforce password history — 4 passwords remembered

  2. Maximum password age — 30 days

  3. Minimum password age — 2 days

  4. Minimum password length — 10 characters

  5. Password must meet complexity requirements — Enabled

  6. Account lockout threshold — 4 invalid logon attempts

  7. Account lockout duration — 60 minutes

  8. Reset account lockout counter after — 40 minutes

notes.title: 3.2.8 - Activity: Performing Threat Intelligence
notes.html:
1. 1. Initial Access

    To prevent threat actors from gaining initial access through phishing, organizations can implement SPF to authenticate email sources. In addition, they can use DMARC to prevent unauthorized use of their domain.

  2. 2. Execution

    To stop the execution of malicious attachments in phishing emails, organizations can use Email quarantine systems to identify and isolate suspicious content. For malicious links, they can deploy URL rewriting to rewrite URLs and protect users from accessing harmful websites.

  3. 3. Privilege Escalation

    To mitigate the risk of privilege escalation in case of a successful phishing attack, organizations can enforce Principle of Least Privilege to limit users' access to sensitive information. They should also regularly review Access controls to ensure that access rights are up-to-date.

  4. 4. Evasion

    To counter evasion techniques used by attackers, organizations can deploy Endpoint Protection solutions to detect and respond to malicious activities in real-time. They can also implement Network analysis to monitor network traffic and detect any unusual patterns.

  5. 5. C2

    To disrupt command and control communication between the compromised system and the attacker, organizations can implement Network segmentation to monitor network traffic. Additionally, they can apply Firewall rules to restrict communication channels used by the attacker.

  6. 6. Persistence and Lateral Movement

    To eliminate persistence mechanisms used by attackers, organizations can regularly update their Security patches to fix known vulnerabilities. They can also deploy MFA to ensure that access to sensitive data requires additional authentication.

  7. 7. Impair Process Controls and Inhibit Response Function

    To hinder lateral movement within the network, organizations can enforce Network segmentation to control the flow of data between systems. They can use IDS to monitor for suspicious activities across the network.

notes.title: 3.4.10 - Create a Honeypot with Pentbox
notes.html:
Lab Steps — Easy Version

1. Create a Honeypot on www_stage

  1. Open Terminal.
  2. Type:

cd pentbox-1.8

  1. Press Enter.
  2. Type:

./pentbox.rb

  1. Press Enter.
  2. Type 2 and press Enter for Network Tools.
  3. Type 3 and press Enter for Honeypot.
  4. Type 1 and press Enter for Fast Auto Configuration.
  5. Confirm you see:

HONEYPOT ACTIVATED ON PORT 80

2. Test the Honeypot from Marketing3

  1. Select Buildings.
  2. Select Building A → Floor 2.
  3. Under Marketing Group B, select Marketing3.
  4. Open Google Chrome.
  5. Enter:

www_stage.corpnet.xyz

  1. Press Enter.
  2. The webpage displays Access denied.

3. Review the Intrusion

  1. Select Building A.
  2. Select Basement.
  3. Select www_stage.
  4. Look at the Pentbox terminal.
  5. Find:

INTRUSION ATTEMPT DETECTED!

  1. The connection shows:

192.168.0.39:50019

192.168.0.39 = IP address
50019 = port number

Lab Questions and Answers

Q1. Which message is displayed?

Answer: Access denied ✅

Q2. What is the IP address associated with the intrusion attempt?

Answer: 192.168.0.39 ✅

How We Got the Answers

Q1: After Marketing3 browsed to www_stage.corpnet.xyz, Chrome displayed Access denied.

Q2: Pentbox recorded the connection and displayed:

INTRUSION ATTEMPT DETECTED! from 192.168.0.39:50019

Therefore, the intrusion attempt came from 192.168.0.39.

Final Check

Honeypot created: ✅
Marketing3 tested the honeypot: ✅
Q1: Access denied: ✅
Q2: 192.168.0.39: ✅
Score: 2/2 questions correct: ✅

  1. Open Terminal.
  2. Type:

cd pentbox-1.8

  1. Press Enter.
  2. Type:

./pentbox.rb

  1. Press Enter.
  2. Type 2 and press Enter for Network Tools.
  3. Type 3 and press Enter for Honeypot.
  4. Type 1 and press Enter for Fast Auto Configuration.
  5. Confirm you see:

HONEYPOT ACTIVATED ON PORT 80

2. Test the Honeypot from Marketing3

  1. Select Buildings.
  2. Select Building A → Floor 2.
  3. Under Marketing Group B, select Marketing3.
  4. Open Google Chrome.
  5. Enter:

www_stage.corpnet.xyz

  1. Press Enter.
  2. The webpage displays Access denied.

3. Review the Intrusion

  1. Select Building A.
  2. Select Basement.
  3. Select www_stage.
  4. Look at the Pentbox terminal.
  5. Find:

INTRUSION ATTEMPT DETECTED!

  1. The connection shows:

192.168.0.39:50019

192.168.0.39 = IP address
50019 = port number

Lab Questions and Answers

Q1. Which message is displayed?

Answer: Access denied ✅

Q2. What is the IP address associated with the intrusion attempt?

Answer: 192.168.0.39 ✅

How We Got the Answers

Q1: After Marketing3 browsed to www_stage.corpnet.xyz, Chrome displayed Access denied.

Q2: Pentbox recorded the connection and displayed:

INTRUSION ATTEMPT DETECTED! from 192.168.0.39:50019

Therefore, the intrusion attempt came from 192.168.0.39.

Final Check

Honeypot created: ✅
Marketing3 tested the honeypot: ✅
Q1: Access denied: ✅
Q2: 192.168.0.39: ✅
Score: 2/2 questions correct: ✅

    2. Type:

    systemctl is-active bluetooth.service

    1. Verify that the service is active.

    Stop service: ✅

notes.html:
Lab Steps — Easy Version

  1. Enable the Anaconda Service

    1. Open Terminal.

    2. At the prompt, type:

    systemctl enable anaconda.service

    1. Press Enter.

    2. Check the service's status:

    systemctl is-enabled anaconda.service

    1. Press Enter.

  2. Disable the VMware Tools Service

    1. At the prompt, type:

    systemctl disable vmtoolsd.service

    1. Press Enter.

    2. Check the service's status:

    systemctl is-enabled vmtoolsd.service

    1. Press Enter.

  3. Final Check

    Enable service: ✅

    systemctl enable anaconda.service

    Check status:

    systemctl is-enabled anaconda.service

    Disable service: ✅

    systemctl disable vmtoolsd.service

    Check status:

    systemctl is-enabled vmtoolsd.service

    Those are the exact commands from the lab explanation.

notes.title: 4.1.7 - Disable Windows Services
notes.html:
Lab Steps — Easy Version

  1. Scan the Network for Port 3389

    1. From the Favorites bar, select Zenmap.
    2. Maximize the window.
    3. In the Command field, type: 
    nmap -p 3389 192.168.0.0/24
    1. Select Scan or press Enter.
    2. Look through the results for a computer showing 3389/tcp open.
    3. The scan identifies:

    192.168.0.34 = Office2

    1. In the top-right corner, select Answer Questions.

  2. Answer Question 1

    Q1. Which computer(s) have port 3389 open? (Select all that apply.)

    Answer: 192.168.0.34 ✅

  3. Scan the Network for Port 5900

    1. Return to Zenmap.
    2. In the Command field, type: 
    nmap -p 5900 192.168.0.0/24
    1. Select Scan or press Enter.
    2. Look for a computer showing 5900/tcp open.
    3. The scan identifies:

    192.168.0.31 = ITAdmin

  4. Answer Question 2

    Q2. Which computer(s) have port 5900 open? (Select all that apply.)

    Answer: 192.168.0.31 ✅

  5. Disable and Stop Remote Desktop Services on Office2

    Port 3389 is being used by Remote Desktop Services (TermServices) on Office2.

    1. From the top navigation tabs, select Floor 1 Overview.
    2. Select Office2.
    3. In the taskbar search field, type:

    Services

    1. Under Best Match, select Services.
    2. Maximize the window.
    3. Find and double-click Remote Desktop Services.
    4. Set Startup Type to Disabled.
    5. Under Service status, select Stop.
    6. Select OK.

  6. Disable and Stop VNC Server on ITAdmin

    Port 5900 is being used by VNC Server (vncserver) on ITAdmin.

    1. Return to Floor 1 Overview.
    2. Select ITAdmin.
    3. In the taskbar search field, type:

    Services

    1. Under Best Match, select Services.
    2. Maximize the window.
    3. Find and double-click VNC Server.
    4. Set Startup Type to Disabled.
    5. Under Service status, select Stop.
    6. Select OK.

  7. Finish the Lab

    1. In the top-right corner, select Answer Questions.
    2. Make sure both questions are answered.
    3. Select Score Lab.

  8. Computer Identification

    IP AddressComputer Name
    192.168.0.30Exec
    192.168.0.31ITAdmin
    192.168.0.32Gst-Lap
    192.168.0.33Office1
    192.168.0.34Office2
    192.168.0.45Support
    192.168.0.46IT-Laptop

  9. Final Check

    Q1: 192.168.0.34 ✅

    Q2: 192.168.0.31 ✅

    Office2
    Port 3389 identified with Zenmap ✅
    Remote Desktop Service disabled ✅
    Remote Desktop Service stopped ✅

    ITAdmin
    Port 5900 identified with Zenmap ✅
    VNC disabled ✅
    VNC stopped ✅

    Lab note: You would also want to remove or uninstall these services.

Lab Steps — Easy Version

  1. View the Linux Processes

    1. From the Favorites bar, select Terminal.

    1. Press Enter.

    3. Look through the process information to answer the lab questions.

  2. Answer the Lab Questions

    In the top-right corner, select Answer Questions.


    Q1. What is the PID for the hald process?

    Answer: 1194 ✅


    Q2. What is the state of the ./shell.elf process?

    Answer: running ✅


    Q3. What is the percentage of memory used by the ./shell.elf process?

    Answer: 3.0 ✅


    Q4. Which command invoked PID 1857?

    Answer: python ✅

    Q3: 3.0 ✅

notes.title: 4.2.9 - Activity: Analyzing Network Infrastructures
notes.html:
Hybrid Cloud — Final Confirmed Notes ✅

12/12 Correct

  1. Benefits, Risks, and Mitigation

    1. Scalability

    Risk: Data Breaches

    Mitigation: Implement Access Controls

    Hybrid cloud allows workloads to be spread between public and private cloud environments, making it easier to scale resources up or down. Because data is spread across multiple environments, there is a greater risk of data breaches. Access controls restrict sensitive data to authorized users.

    2. Flexibility

    Risk: Data Fragmentation

    Mitigation: Data Backup and Recovery

    Hybrid cloud gives a business flexibility to choose which environment should run each workload. This can cause data to become spread across different systems, formats, or locations. Backup and recovery helps protect against data loss.

    3. Geographic Distribution

    Risk: Legal Implications

    Mitigation: Contractual Agreements

    Applications and data can be distributed across multiple geographic locations, which can improve performance, reduce latency, and help with business continuity. Different locations can have different laws and regulations, so businesses should clearly understand their contractual obligations with cloud providers and vendors.

  2. Public vs. Private vs. Hybrid

    Public Cloud

    Best Benefit: Greater Scalability ✅

    Resources can quickly scale up or down as demand changes.

    Private Cloud

    Best Benefit: Increased Control ✅

    More control over resources and workloads can improve security and resource management.

    Hybrid Cloud

    Disadvantage: Increased Complexity ✅

    Managing both public and private environments makes the infrastructure more complicated.

  3. Easy Way to Remember

    Scalability → Data Breaches → Access Controls

    Flexibility → Data Fragmentation → Backup & Recovery

    Geographic Distribution → Legal Implications → Contractual Agreements

    Public = Greater Scalability

    Private = Increased Control

    Hybrid = Increased Complexity

    These are now confirmed by the 12/12 TestOut score.

versions.title: 4.2.9 - Activity: Analyzing Network Infrastructures
versions.html:
Hybrid Cloud — Notes

  1. Hybrid Cloud Benefits, Risks, and Solutions

    1. Scalability
    Risk: Data Breaches
    Solution: Implement Access Controls

    A hybrid cloud makes it easier to increase resources when the company needs them. Since data can be stored across different environments, there is a higher risk of data breaches. Access controls help make sure only authorized users can access sensitive data.

    2. Flexibility
    Risk: Data Fragmentation
    Solution: Data Backup and Recovery

    A hybrid cloud gives a company flexibility to decide whether workloads should run in the public or private cloud. However, this can spread data across different systems and locations. Backup and recovery helps protect the data if something happens.

    3. Geographic Distribution
    Risk: Legal Implications
    Solution: Contractual Agreements

versions.title: 4.2.9 - Activity: Analyzing Network Infrastructures
versions.html:
Hybrid Cloud Infrastructure — Notes

  1. Hybrid Cloud

    A hybrid cloud combines public cloud and private cloud environments. It gives a company more flexibility because it can decide which services and data should stay private and which can be moved to the public cloud.

  2. Benefits, Risks, and Solutions

    1. Better Performance
    Risk: Decreased Accessibility
    Solution: Increase the Number of Servers

    Having more servers can improve availability and help prevent one overloaded server from slowing everything down.

    2. Flexibility
    Risk: Data Fragmentation
    Solution: Data Backup and Recovery

    A hybrid cloud lets a company move and use resources in different environments, but this can cause data to become spread out. Backups help protect and recover that data.

    3. Geographic Distribution
    Risk: Legal Implications
    Solution: Contractual Agreements

    Cloud data and services can exist in different locations. Different locations may have different laws, so contracts can clearly define responsibilities and requirements.

  3. Public vs. Private vs. Hybrid Cloud

    Public Cloud
    Best Benefit: Greater Scalability
    It is easier to increase or decrease cloud resources when needed.

    Private Cloud
    Best Benefit: Increased Control
    The organization has more control over its systems, data, and security.

    Hybrid Cloud
    Main Disadvantage: Increased Complexity
    Managing both public and private cloud systems together can be harder than managing only one type.

  4. Easy Way to Remember

    Public = Scalability

    Private = Control

    Hybrid = Flexibility, but more Complexity

notes.title: 4.5.9 - Log Events with pfSense
notes.html:
Lab Steps — Easy Version

  1. Sign In to pfSense

    1. Open the pfSense Management console.

    2. In Username, enter:

    admin

    1. In Password, enter:

    P@ssw0rd

    The last character is a zero (0).

    1. Select SIGN IN or press Enter.

  2. Open System Logs and Answer Question 1

    1. From the top menu, select Status.

    2. Select System Logs.

    3. In the top-right, select Answer Questions.

    Q1. What is the maximum number of logs that can be displayed?

    Answer: 50 ✅

  3. Configure the General Log Settings

    1. Under the Status breadcrumb, select Settings.

    2. Find GUI Log Entries.

    3. Change it to:

    25

    1. Find Log file size.

    2. Enter:

    250000

    This sets each log file to a maximum of 250,000 bytes (250 KB).

  4. Enable Remote Logging

    1. Scroll down to Remote Logging Options.

    2. Check Enable Remote Logging.

    3. Configure:

    Source address: Default (any)

    IP protocol: IPv4

    Remote log servers: 192.168.0.10

    1. Under Remote Syslog Contents, select only:

    System Events ✅

    Firewall Events ✅

    1. Select Save.

  5. Check the New Log Setting

    1. Under the Status breadcrumb, select System.

    2. Open Answer Questions if needed.

    Q2. What is the maximum number of logs that can be displayed after configuring the system log settings?

    Answer: 25 ✅

    1. Select Score Lab.

  6. Final Check

    Q1: 50 ✅

    GUI Log Entries: 25 ✅

    Log file size: 250000 bytes ✅

    Remote Logging: Enabled ✅

    Source Address: Default (any) ✅

    IP Protocol: IPv4 ✅

    Remote Log Server: 192.168.0.10 ✅

    System Events: Selected ✅

    Firewall Events: Selected ✅

    Q2: 25 ✅

    Important correction: The original maximum number of logs is 50, not 75. After changing GUI Log Entries, the answer becomes 25.

notes.title: 4.5.10 - Evaluate Event Logs in pfSense
notes.html:
Lab Steps — Easy Version

  1. Sign In to pfSense

    1. Open the pfSense Management Console.

    2. In the Username field, enter:

    admin

    1. In the Password field, enter:

    P@ssw0rd

    The last character is a zero (0).

    1. Select SIGN IN or press Enter.

  2. Open the DHCP Logs

    1. From the pfSense menu bar, select Status.

    2. Select System Logs.

    3. Under the Status breadcrumb, select DHCP.

    4. Examine the DHCP log entries.

    5. Look specifically for duplicate DHCPACK entries.

  3. Answer the Lab Question

    In the top-right corner, select Answer Questions.

    Q1. What, if any, indication is there of an on-path attack?

    Answer: There are two DHCPACK entries with the same IP and MAC address. ✅

  4. How We Got the Answer

    The DHCP logs showed two identical DHCPACK entries for:

    IP Address: 192.168.1.110

    MAC Address: 00:15:5d:01:23:55

    Seeing two DHCPACK entries with the same IP and MAC address is the indication of a possible on-path (man-in-the-middle) attack in this lab.

  5. Final Check

    Location: Status → System Logs → DHCP ✅

    What to look for: Duplicate DHCPACK entries ✅

    Correct Answer: There are two DHCPACK entries with the same IP and MAC address. ✅

notes.title: 4.5.11 - Evaluate Windows Log Files
notes.html:
Lab Steps — Easy Version

  1. Get a List of the Current Event Logs

    1. Right-click Start.
    2. Select Windows PowerShell (Admin).
    3. Maximize the window.
    4. Type:
    Get-Eventlog -logname *
    1. Press Enter.
    2. In the top-right, select Answer Questions.

  2. Question 1

    Q1. How many event logs are being captured on Office1?

    Answer: 7 ✅

  3. View the System Log

    1. Go back to PowerShell.
    2. You can use the UP arrow key to reuse your previous command.
    3. Type:
    Get-Eventlog -logname system
    1. Press Enter.
    2. Examine the last two entries.

  4. Question 2

    Q2. Which entry types were used for the last two log entries of the system log?

    Answer: Warning, Information ✅

    Select both:

    Warning ✅

    Information ✅

  5. View the Application Log

    1. If you want to clear the PowerShell screen first, type:
    CLS
    1. Press Enter.
    2. Type:
    Get-Eventlog -logname application
    1. Press Enter.
    2. Examine the last entry.

  6. Question 3

    Q3. What was the source of the last error entry listed in the application log?

    Answer: Application ✅

  7. Question 4

    Q4. What is the InstanceID for the last application log entry?

    Answer: 1085 ✅

  8. Question 5

    Q5. For which program did the last error message create an entry in the application log?

    Answer: Notepad++ ✅

  9. View the Security Log

    1. Go back to PowerShell.
    2. Type:
    Get-Eventlog -logname security
    1. Press Enter.
    2. Examine the security entries.

  10. Question 6

    Q6. Which security entries might be of MOST concern and may warrant further evaluation?

    Answer: An account failed to log on.... ✅

    1. Select Score Lab.

  11. Final Check

    Q1: 7 ✅

    Q2: Warning, Information ✅

    Q3: Application ✅

    Q4: 1085 ✅

    Q5: Notepad++ ✅

    Q6: An account failed to log on.... ✅

  12. Commands to Remember

    Get-Eventlog -logname *
Get-Eventlog -logname system
Get-Eventlog -logname application
Get-Eventlog -logname security

    These answers are now confirmed by the official TestOut Task Summary.

versions.title: 4.5.11 - Evaluate Windows Log Files
versions.html:
## Lab Steps — Easy Version

### 1. Get a List of the Current Event Logs

1. Right-click **Start**.
2. Select **Windows PowerShell (Admin)**.
3. Maximize the window.
4. Type:

```powershell
Get-Eventlog -logname *
```

5. Press **Enter**.
6. In the top-right, select **Answer Questions**.

### Question 1

**Q1. How many event logs are being captured on Office1?**

**Answer: 7** ✅

### 2. View the System Log

1. Go back to **PowerShell**.
2. You can use the **UP arrow key** to reuse your previous command.
3. Type:

```powershell
Get-Eventlog -logname system
```

4. Press **Enter**.
5. Examine the **last two entries**.

### Question 2

**Q2. Which entry types were used for the last two log entries of the system log?**

**Answer: Warning, Information** ✅

Select both:

**Warning** ✅
**Information** ✅

### 3. View the Application Log

1. If you want to clear the PowerShell screen first, type:

```powershell
CLS
```

2. Press **Enter**.
3. Type:

```powershell
Get-Eventlog -logname application
```

4. Press **Enter**.
5. Examine the **last entry**.

### Question 3

**Q3. What was the source of the last error entry listed in the application log?**

**Answer: Application** ✅

### Question 4

**Q4. What is the InstanceID for the last application log entry?**

**Answer: 1085** ✅

### Question 5

**Q5. For which program did the last error message create an entry in the application log?**

**Answer: Notepad++** ✅

### 4. View the Security Log

1. Go back to **PowerShell**.
2. Type:

```powershell
Get-Eventlog -logname security
```

3. Press **Enter**.
4. Examine the security entries.

### Question 6

**Q6. Which security entries might be of MOST concern and may warrant further evaluation?**

**Answer: An account failed to log on....** ✅

5. Select **Score Lab**.

### Final Check

**Q1:** 7 ✅
**Q2:** Warning, Information ✅
**Q3:** Application ✅
**Q4:** 1085 ✅
**Q5:** Notepad++ ✅
**Q6:** An account failed to log on.... ✅

### Commands to Remember

```powershell
Get-Eventlog -logname *
Get-Eventlog -logname system
Get-Eventlog -logname application
Get-Eventlog -logname security
```

These answers are now **confirmed by the official TestOut Task Summary**.
